The short version

You do not need an account to read YonoappDex. We do not run advertising trackers, we do not build personal profiles of our visitors, and we do not sell anyone's data. This page explains the small amount of technical data that passes through the site when you visit or write to us, and what rights you have over it.

Who runs the site and the laws we follow

YonoappDex is managed by its site administration, which acts as the Data Fiduciary for any personal data we receive. We operate this policy in line with India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) and the Information Technology Act, 2000. Our designated Grievance Officer is Govardhan Das.

What happens when you visit a page

When you open a page on YonoappDex, your browser connects through our security and edge network provider (Cloudflare) and our web hosting servers. Like all websites, this requires basic connection details to pass through: your IP address, browser type, operating system, the page you asked for, and the date and time of the request.

Why connection details are needed

Because an IP address can count as personal data under the law, we limit how it is used:

  • Delivering the site: Sending the text and layout of the page back to your phone or computer.
  • Security and bot blocking: Stopping automated scrapers, spam attacks, and denial-of-service traffic before they break the site.
  • Basic totals: Seeing overall visit counts (such as which game pages are read most) in combined totals that do not identify any individual visitor.

Where server logs are processed

Our hosting and security providers handle traffic on global edge servers, which means basic connection logs may be processed on servers inside or outside India in line with their own security policies and Indian law. We do not use these logs to identify you by name or track what you do on other websites.

Cookies and small browser files

YonoappDex does not use third-party advertising cookies or cross-site tracking pixels.

Security tokens and site preferences

Our security provider (Cloudflare) may place a small temporary file or token in your browser to verify that your connection is coming from a real person rather than an automated bot. The site may also use basic browser storage on your device to remember simple choices, such as closing an information banner.

Controlling your browser settings

You can clear or block cookies and site storage at any time in your browser settings (such as in Google Chrome, Safari, or Firefox). The directory will still work, though our security system may ask you to complete a human-check prompt more often.

Images and links to other websites

YonoappDex writes about games made by outside developers and links to official stores under our Download Policy.

App icons and screenshots

Some game icons or promotional screenshots shown on our profiles load directly from the official app store or the developer's own website. When your browser loads an image hosted on an outside server, that server receives your IP address and basic browser details under its own privacy rules.

When you click an external link

When you click a download link or store link, you leave YonoappDex. We show a clear notice before you go. Once you arrive on Google Play, the Apple App Store, or a developer's website, their privacy policy applies. Free games often ask for phone numbers, device permissions, or payment details once installed; we do not control or receive any of that data.

When you send a report or email us

You can use the Report this game button on any page without creating an account or giving your name. If you choose to include your email address, or if you write to support@yonoappdex.com, we receive whatever details you send us—such as your message, email address, screenshots, or ownership documents.

How we handle your message

  • Purpose: We use your message solely to verify your report, update our game pages, or handle legal and copyright requests under our Report and Removal Policy.
  • No marketing or sharing: We never sell or rent your email address, and we never pass your contact details to game developers or marketers.
  • Checking with developers: If we need to ask a developer about a reported bug or rule change, we share only the substance of the issue without revealing who reported it. We only disclose personal details if required by Indian law or a valid court or government order.
  • How long we keep it: Please do not send sensitive personal details (such as bank numbers or government IDs) in a report. Once a ticket or legal claim is resolved, we archive or delete the messages once they are no longer needed for legal compliance.

Children's privacy

YonoappDex is a public information directory. Because we do not use user accounts or sign-up forms, we do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 18, and we do not track or target young visitors with ads in line with Section 9 of the DPDP Act, 2023.

If you are under 18, please ask a parent or guardian before emailing us or sending a report with your contact details. If a parent or guardian discovers that a child has sent us personal information, write to us and we will delete it straight away.

Your rights and Grievance Officer

Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, if you have shared personal data with us (for example, by emailing us), you have the right to:

  • Ask whether we hold personal information about you and get a summary of it.
  • Ask us to correct or update inaccurate details.
  • Withdraw your consent and ask us to erase your messages and email address, unless we are legally required to keep a record of a formal dispute.
  • Register a grievance with us, and if it is not resolved through our grievance process, approach the Data Protection Board of India.

Games should be fun

Most people open a Yono game or casual app to unwind for ten minutes on the bus or relax after a long day. That is what free mobile games are built for. However, games are also engineered with rewards, streaks, and prompts designed to keep you tapping.

This guide offers practical boundaries to help ensure gaming stays an enjoyable break rather than taking over your day. You can also read more about our safety standards on our Ethics & Safety page.

Managing your time and screen habits

It is very easy to lose track of time when playing quick puzzle, arcade, or card games. A few simple habits keep screen time under control:

  • Set a timer: Decide how long you want to play before you open an app. When the timer goes off, close the game.
  • Take regular breaks: Step away from the screen every thirty minutes to rest your eyes and stretch.
  • Keep gaming out of bed: Avoid playing right before sleep so your mind has time to wind down.
  • Watch for warning signs: If you find yourself skipping meals, losing sleep, or neglecting studies or work because of a game, that is your cue to take a break for the day.

In-app purchases, ads, and virtual coins

Free-to-play games earn money by showing ads and selling virtual items like extra lives, custom skins, card decks, or coin packs. Small purchases add up fast.

  • Set a monthly budget: If you buy virtual items, decide on a strict limit before each month begins.
  • Lock store purchases: Go into your Google Play or Apple App Store settings and turn on password or biometric (fingerprint or face) verification for every single purchase.
  • Virtual coins are not real money: Winning virtual chips or coins in a card game or free casino-style game has zero cash value and cannot be withdrawn. It does not mean you will win at real-world activities, and it does not make gambling safe.

Protecting your personal details

A legitimate free mobile game will never ask for sensitive personal data or financial credentials.

  • Never share banking details: A free game has no business asking for your bank account number, UPI PIN, credit card CVV, or phone OTPs.
  • Beware of support scams: If someone messages you on Telegram, WhatsApp, or social media claiming to be game support and asks for your password or a verification code, block them immediately.
  • Check permissions: When installing an app from the official store, review what it asks to access. A card, puzzle, or board game has zero reason to read your SMS messages, call logs, or contacts.

Avoiding fake apps and "mod" scams

Popular mobile games are frequently targeted by scam websites and social media videos offering "hacked APKs", "unlimited coins", or "winning tricks".

Those modified files are a primary way hackers distribute malware, steal personal data, and take over phones. Always install games strictly through official store links or verified developer sites. If you spot a game that offers cash payouts or asks you to pay a fee to withdraw winnings, leave it alone and report it using our Report and Removal Policy.

Safety for parents and guardians

Many households share mobile devices with children. If younger family members play games on your phone, take a few precautions:

  • Use parental controls: Set up Google Family Link or Apple Screen Time to manage daily play schedules and require parent approval for new app downloads.
  • Secure financial apps: Keep UPI apps, banking passwords, and saved payment cards locked behind a secure PIN that children do not know.
  • Watch out for stranger chat: Many digital board and card games feature online multiplayer rooms with live text or voice chat. Check our game profiles before letting children play online.
  • vTeach kids about ads: Children often struggle to tell the difference between actual game buttons and pop-up advertisements. Talk to them about avoiding accidental clicks on ad banners.

When gaming stops being fun (Helplines in India)

If playing games begins to interfere with your sleep, studies, career, or relationships—or if you find yourself hiding how much time or money you spend—it is important to talk to someone. Confidential, professional help is available across India:

Mental health and gaming overuse support

  • Tele-MANAS: Call 14416 or 1800-891-4416 (free, 24/7 helpline by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, available in multiple Indian languages). Read more on the official Tele-MANAS Portal.
  • KIRAN Helpline: Call 1800-599-0019 for 24/7 mental health and psychological support.
  • NIMHANS SHUT Clinic: Based in Bengaluru, the Service for Healthy Use of Technology clinic offers specialized guidance for technology and gaming overuse. Visit the NIMHANS Official Website for details.

Reporting cyber fraud and financial scams

If you or someone you know has been cheated by an online scam, fake app, or fraudulent payment demand:

  • File an official report immediately on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.
  • Call the national cyber helpline at 1930.

Please note that YonoappDex is an independent information directory; we cannot close player accounts, recover lost funds, or resolve disputes with game developers. For game-specific support, contact the developer directly through their official store page.

To report a broken link, unsafe app, or directory mistake, use the Report this game button on any profile or write directly to our Grievance Officer, Govardhan Das, at support@yonoappdex.com.

Why reports matter

We work hard to keep YonoappDex accurate and up to date, but game developers change their apps, update their links, or shift their features without telling us. Because we do not test every game every day, a report from a visitor or a rights owner is often the first sign that something on our site needs attention.

This page explains how to send us a report, what issues you can raise, and how we handle them. We operate our removal process to follow Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and Rule 3(2) of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.

How to send a report

You do not need to create an account or sign in to let us know about an issue.

  • On any game page: Click the Report this game button located near the profile. Choose the type of problem, add a short note explaining what is wrong, and hit send.
  • By email: For legal notices, copyright claims, trademark objections, or reports requiring attached screenshots or documents, write directly to support@yonoappdex.com.

What you can report

  1. Real-money features: A listed game has added cash deposits, betting, or rewards that can be withdrawn or swapped for money, vouchers, or real-world prizes. (We strictly prohibit real-money apps).
  2. A broken or hijacked link: The outbound link takes you somewhere other than the official store page, starts an unexpected file download, or leads to a look-alike clone.
  3. Malware or security risks: A game or its linked site is attempting to steal personal data, trick users, or distribute malicious files.
  4. Outdated or incorrect information: The version is old, the developer name is wrong, game rules have changed entirely, or the app no longer exists on the official store.
  5. Copyright or trademark claims: A brand name, logo, image, or text on our site belongs to you or your company, protected under the Copyright Act, 1957 or the Trade Marks Act, 1999.

Our "Link-First" safety response

When a report involves safety, real-money features, or hijacked links, we follow a strict link-first policy to protect our visitors:

  1. Immediate quarantine: If a report flags real-money gameplay, malware, or a compromised link, we take the outbound download link down straight away—often within hours—while we investigate the details.
  2. Review and correction: We examine the game's public store listing, developer website, and published rules to verify what changed.
  3. Restoration or removal: If our investigation shows the report was mistaken or that the link is safe and official, we put the download link back. If the report is confirmed true, the link stays down permanently and the game is removed from the directory.
  4. Safety notices: If a game or linked site is confirmed to be malicious or scam-oriented, we may keep a clear warning label on the profile so other visitors are alerted.

Our response timelines (SLAs)

We treat every report with urgency and follow structured timelines:

  • Acknowledgment: We acknowledge receipt of your report within 24 hours.
  • Link removal for urgent reports: We aim to remove download links for confirmed real-money, malware, or hijacked-link reports within 24 hours, often sooner.
  • Final resolution: We complete our investigation and provide a final answer or correction within 15 days of receiving the report.

Requirements for developers and rights owners

If you own a game we have listed or hold rights to material on our site and believe an error has been made, please write to our Grievance Officer with sufficient detail:

  • The exact URL of the page on YonoappDex.
  • A clear explanation of what is incorrect, missing, or infringing.
  • Proof of ownership or authorization (such as trademark registration numbers, domain ownership records, or an official company authorization letter).
  • A good-faith statement confirming that the information provided in your notice is accurate.

We require this proof to prevent our report tool from being misused by competitors trying to remove legitimate directory listings.

What we cannot do

YonoappDex is an independent information directory; we do not develop games, manage player accounts, or process financial transactions.

  • We cannot recover money lost in a fraudulent app, issue refunds, or unlock banned game accounts.
  • If you have fallen victim to online cyber fraud or financial cheating, please file an official complaint immediately on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal or call the national cyber helpline at 1930. We strongly urge you to report fraud to the authorities alongside notifying us.

In compliance with the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, our designated Grievance Officer is:

Why we built YonoappDex

Type "Yono games" into a search engine and you get a mess. You see copied websites, fake download buttons, modded APK files with the same name from different makers, and blogs that claim every game is the best just to get your click.

Because of that clutter, ordinary players end up installing apps they know nothing about from sources they cannot verify. We built YonoappDex to fix that. We wanted one clean, straightforward place where a game is explained in plain words and its real maker is easy to check before anyone hits install.

What we do

YonoappDex is a free information directory. Our motto is simple: know the game before you download it. We sort free Yono games into clear categories—card, casual, board, arcade, and free casino-style—and write a dedicated profile for each title.

What goes into a game profile

  • Plain-English rules: What kind of game it is and how a round actually plays.
  • Ads and purchases: How the free game makes money, including ad frequency and in-app item sales.
  • Phone permissions: What access the app asks for on your device, flagging anything unusual like contacts or SMS access.
  • Chat and online rooms: Whether the game lets players talk to strangers, so parents can check before handing over a phone.
  • Maker and review date: Who built the game, the version we looked at, and the exact date we last checked the facts.

How we review and label games

We write every profile from public records: official listings on Google Play and the Apple App Store, verified developer websites, and published game rules. We do not inspect private source code, decompile APK files, or play-test every level of every game.

What our labels mean

  • Official Source Confirmed (Green Tick): We checked the developer's identity, confirmed the game is free to play without real-money cash-outs, and matched our link to the official store page or developer website. Only these pages get a download link.
  • Source Not Verified: We could not confirm where the game comes from. We publish the information so you know what it is, but we leave the download link out.
  • Under Review: We are still checking the details, or we have temporarily removed the link after a user report.

You can read our full step-by-step process on How We Review Games.

Editorial independence

We do not sell rankings, green ticks, or favourable reviews. A developer cannot pay us to list a game, hide a permission warning, or push their app to the top of a category. Games earn a link solely by being free to play and having an official source we can confirm.

If a developer or rights owner asks us to change something on a profile, we update it only when the public facts support the change.

What we are not

To keep things completely clear for visitors, developers, and regulators:

No connection with SBI or YONO banking

YonoappDex is an independent game directory. We have no connection, affiliation, or partnership with State Bank of India (SBI), the official YONO SBI banking application, or any bank or financial service. We use the word "Yono" only in its common search sense to describe a category of mobile games, as explained in our Legal Notice.

Not an APK host or game studio

We do not make games, run game servers, or handle player accounts. We also do not host, store, or share APK files or installation packages on our servers. When a link is shown, it takes you straight to the official store or developer site under our Download Policy.

No real-money gambling

We do not list real-money games. If a game offers cash deposits, betting, or coins that can be withdrawn or swapped for money or vouchers, it is kept off this site.

How we handle reports and get in touch

Developers update apps all the time without telling us. If you spot a broken link, outdated information, or a listed game that has added real-money features, click the Report this game button on the game page. No account is needed. For safety and real-money reports, we aim to take the link down within 24 hours and check the details afterwards under our Report and Removal Policy.

Contact and Grievance Officer

We operate in line with the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. For general questions, game requests, corrections, or formal legal notices, write to us:

support@yonoappdex.com

Our ethics: how we keep this site honest

People come to YonoappDex because search results for Yono games are full of copied sites, fake download buttons, and blogs that call every app the best. To be useful, our directory has to stay honest and independent.

No paid rankings or bought labels

We do not take money from developers to list a game, give it a green tick, or push it to the top of a category. Every app is checked using the same rules, which you can read on How We Review Games.

No real-money games

We only list free-to-play games where virtual coins, chips, or points stay inside the game and have no cash value. If an app lets players deposit money, bet, or cash out winnings or vouchers, it does not belong on YonoappDex.

Clear facts, not hype

We write from public records—store pages, developer websites, and published game rules. We do not use fake star ratings or made-up user reviews. Every game page shows the exact date we last checked it, and if we cannot confirm who made a game, we say so plainly and leave the download link out.

Fast corrections when things change

Developers often update their apps without warning. If a visitor reports that a listed game has added real-money features, moved to a shady link, or started acting unsafely, we take the download link down first—usually within 24 hours—and check the facts afterwards.

Phone and download safety

We do not host, store, or share APK files. Even when you follow an official link from our site, a few simple habits will keep your phone and data safe.

Verify before you install

  • Match the developer name: Check that the maker listed on the store page matches the name on our profile. Popular card and board games have many look-alikes.
  • Check phone permissions: A simple card, puzzle, or arcade game has no reason to ask for your SMS messages, call logs, or contacts. If it asks for more than it needs, do not install it.
  • Skip "mod" and "hacked" files: Avoid websites, Telegram groups, or videos offering "unlimited coins", "unlocked VIP", or modded APKs. Those files are one of the most common ways to put malware on your phone.

Protect your money and accounts

A legitimate free game will never ask for your bank details, UPI PIN, or a phone OTP. Never share those with anyone claiming to be from a game's support team or promising a prize.

Healthy play and spending limits

Free games are built to hold your attention and sell small upgrades. Keeping a few boundaries in place helps make sure gaming stays a fun break.

Time and habits

Games use daily streaks, timers, and "one more round" prompts to keep you tapping. Decide how long you want to play before you open an app, take breaks every half hour, and avoid playing right before sleep. If a game starts getting in the way of sleep, study, or work, take a step back.

In-app purchases and ads

Small purchases for extra coins, lives, or boosts add up fast. Set a monthly spending limit if you buy in-game items, and turn on password or fingerprint verification for every purchase in your Google Play or App Store settings. Remember that winning virtual coins in a free casino-style or card game says nothing about real gambling.

Safety for parents and younger players

Many people share a family phone with children. Before handing over a device with games installed, check a few settings.

Device controls and purchases

Use Google Family Link or Apple Screen Time to set daily play limits and require parent approval before a new app is installed. Keep UPI apps, banking passwords, and saved cards locked behind a PIN that children do not know.

Online rooms and stranger chat

Many digital board and card games include public rooms with live text or voice chat. On our game pages, we note when a game lets players talk to strangers so you can check before a child plays. It also helps to show younger players how in-game ads work, since many ads look just like a real "play" or "collect" button.

Help when gaming stops being fun

If gaming is hurting your sleep, work, studies, or family life—or if you have been cheated by a fake app—free and official help is available in India.

Wellbeing and gaming overuse

  • Tele-MANAS: Call 14416 or 1800-891-4416 (free, 24/7, available in major Indian languages).
  • KIRAN Helpline: Call 1800-599-0019 for 24/7 confidential mental health support.
  • NIMHANS SHUT Clinic (Bengaluru): Specialised help for technology and gaming overuse.

Cyber fraud and unsafe apps

If an app or website has tricked you into paying money or stolen your details, report it on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal or call 1930 right away.

To report a bad link, an unsafe app, or a mistake on YonoappDex, use the Report this game button on any profile or write to our Grievance Officer, Govardhan Das, at support@yonoappdex.com.
